title: The monk who bowed to everyone

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? is there someone you find it hard to respect right now?
options: that’s heavy to carry. this story is for you.
most of us have one. listen to this.
lovely. keep this one for the day you do.

steps.line: Long ago, the Lotus Sutra says, there lived a monk who did something unusual. He bowed to everyone he met.
To each person he said: “I deeply respect you. I would never look down on you. You will all walk the way and become buddhas.”
Not everyone liked it. Some people got angry. “Who is this fool,” they said, “telling us we’ll be buddhas?”

steps.q: Some of them throw sticks and stones at him. What does he do?
o: He stops bowing to the angry ones
He bows lower, and takes the blows
He backs away, and calls it out again
steps.why: He keeps his distance, and keeps his respect. The Lotus Sutra says he ran off a way and still shouted the same words from afar.

steps.line: When they threw sticks and stones, he stepped back out of reach, and called out the same words again.

steps.q: Why did he keep bowing to people who were rude to him?
o: He hoped guilt would make them stop
He saw the buddha they could become
His teacher had ordered him to
steps.why: The Lotus Sutra is a Mahayana scripture, loved in East Asia. Many there teach that anyone can wake up. He bowed to that, not to how people behaved that day.

steps.line: He kept bowing for years. Later, the Buddha told this story and said: that monk was me, in a life long ago.

steps.q: The Lotus Sutra notes something odd about this monk’s practice. What was it?
o: He never read or chanted the sutras
He never once sat to meditate
He refused to live in any temple
steps.why: The sutra says he did not spend his time reading or reciting the sutras. He simply went about bowing. His whole practice was respect.

steps.line: Today, in temples around the world, many Buddhists bow three times: to the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Match each bow to what it’s for.
steps.why: Together they’re called the three jewels, or the triple refuge. Buddhists of every school, Theravada and Mahayana alike, take refuge in them.

say: when buddhists bow three times, it’s to the three jewels: the buddha, the dharma and the sangha. the statue is a reminder, like a photo of someone you love.
and like the monk in the story, many teachers say the bow is to the possibility of waking up, in the buddha and in anyone.

steps.q: The people who mocked him gave him a nickname, from the words he always said. What do you think it was?
steps.why: Never Disparaging: the one who never looks down on anyone. They meant it as mockery. It became his name.

today.say: today, when someone tests your patience, try his bow on the inside. quietly think: you could wake up too. and if you’d like to try three real bows, at home or at a temple, that’s yours to choose.
options: that’s the bow he made every day.
I’d like to try three bows
palms together, three times. the three jewels.
